title: Implement lightweight recording history index
description:
Create a lightweight JSON-backed recording history index that tracks Abracapture capture outputs and their sidecar metadata. The index must support append, removal, and chronological listing without becoming a media library or database project.

Before editing, inspect:
- src/recording/RecordingSink.hpp for the CaptureResult struct (final file path, format, sample rate, duration, provenance) that RecordingEntry wraps.
- Any existing history or index files under src/
- CMakeLists.txt for the src/history/ source group pattern

Do not infer APIs, schemas, behavior, or file contents; inspect the referenced files first.

Implementation:
1. Create src/history/RecordingIndex.hpp declaring a RecordingEntry struct (file path, format, sample rate, bit depth, channels, duration, timestamp, native-vs-converted flag, optional sidecar path) and a RecordingIndex class with append(), remove(), entries(), load(), save() methods.
2. Create src/history/RecordingIndex.cpp implementing JSON serialization/deserialization using QJsonDocument. Store the index file at a configurable path (default: QStandardPaths::AppDataLocation + "/history.json"). Guard file I/O with QSaveFile for atomic writes.
3. Ensure load() handles missing or corrupt index files gracefully (empty index, no crash). Ensure entries() returns newest-first order.

STRICT FILE SCOPE: Create or modify ONLY the files listed in this task's allowed_write_paths.
acceptance_criteria: src/history/RecordingIndex.hpp exists and declares RecordingEntry struct and RecordingIndex class
src/history/RecordingIndex.cpp exists and implements JSON load/save with QJsonDocument
RecordingIndex::append() adds a RecordingEntry and persists to disk
RecordingIndex::entries() returns entries in newest-first chronological order
load() on a missing or corrupt index file produces an empty index without crashing
Atomic write uses QSaveFile or equivalent safe-write pattern
No file outside the task's allowed_write_paths is created or modified
forbidden_changes: implement a database or SQL-backed store

allowed: choose JSON field names for RecordingEntry serialization
choose default index file location under QStandardPaths
forbidden: introduce SQLite or any database dependency
add media scanning or file-system watching
